dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The 31-May cluster contains 17 annual rows/$1,506.29: DLR-104 has 8/$723.42 and DLR-219 has 9/$782.87; effective dates run May 1–28 while posting is 31 May."
"DF-00020 and DF-00040 accepted all 17/17 rows, report 0 duplicate source-event IDs, and reconcile cash to ledger with $0.00 difference."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The anomaly is best explained by contractual month-end batching: the 17 flagged annual renewals have May effective dates but were posted on 31 May."
"the dealer transaction date is retained as effective_event_date while month-end is used as posted_at."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Manipulated reporting — not supported by the supplied evidence."
"However, this does not independently prove that every underlying customer entitlement/revenue-recognition event occurred, so fraud or intent should not be claimed impossible."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "The material unknown is whether the 17 transactions produced the intended customer entitlement/revenue-recognition event."
"Run one read-only reconciliation of the 17 flagged source_event_ids against the downstream entitlement/recognition ledger; make no source-data or accounting changes."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "A read-only match of the 17 source_event_id values to downstream entitlement/recognition records would resolve this."
"Report the affected cohort using both effective_event_date and posted_at so month-end batching cannot be mistaken for a sudden commercial spike."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The anomaly is best explained by contractual month-end batching" is a well-supported inference, but the email corroborates the permitted process rather than independently proving that every flagged transaction was generated through that process.

The statement that downstream entitlement/revenue-recognition records would resolve the issue is directionally appropriate, but a matching record would corroborate posting and entitlement processing rather than by itself establish the absence of every possible accounting or customer-level error. No material unsupported conclusion is presented because the submission explicitly preserves this uncertainty.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A genuine duplicate or misapplied entitlement/revenue-recognition event could still exist despite unique source_event_id values and zero cash-to-ledger difference. The analyst handled this appropriately by identifying it as the key unknown and proposing a targeted downstream reconciliation, while also addressing pipeline defect and manipulation hypotheses.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Execute and report the proposed read-only entitlement/recognition reconciliation for all 17 source_event_ids, including duplicate, missing, and amount/customer mismatches, before treating the no-escalation conclusion as final.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South CareDesk tickets fell from 184 in April to 104 in June (-43.5%), while North changed 168→170, East 98→102, and West 147→169."
"The pilot starts 10 May; South Legacy has 442 IVR sessions/222 cases (50.2%), while Nova has 2,709 sessions/94 cases (3.47%)."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The observed fall in South CareDesk cases is not sufficient evidence of improved customer experience because Nova materially changed the probability that an IVR session becomes a CareDesk case."
"sessions ending before authentication are excluded from CareDesk case reporting"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Service-event presence does not prove unchanged complaint demand, but it contradicts treating the ticket decline alone as evidence that operational problems disappeared."
"The key unknown is whether Nova sessions that do not create CareDesk cases genuinely resolve the customer's issue or merely terminate/avoid case creation."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand NovaIVR nationally; continue the South pilot only under a corrected outcome-measurement design."
"Run one read-only session-to-outcome linkage for South... Keep national expansion on hold."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "for every Nova session, match subsequent 24/72-hour CareDesk cases or repeat contacts, including sessions ending before authentication."
"What exact event creates a CareDesk case in Nova, and how does that rule differ from Legacy? Please provide the rule/version and counts by terminal outcome."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Nova materially changed the probability that an IVR session becomes a CareDesk case" is directionally supported by the observed pre/post rates, but it is phrased causally; the comparison could also reflect differences in session composition or eligibility unless those are controlled.

"IVR-origin case volume itself did not fall materially" is reasonable on the reported daily counts, but it would be stronger with uncertainty intervals, exposure-adjusted rates, and an explicit definition of the pre/post windows.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest benign alternative—that fewer tickets could reflect genuinely improved service or resolution—by preserving it as an unknown and proposing downstream repeat-contact and sampled-call validation. It also noted that incidents do not by themselves prove unchanged complaint demand. A remaining alternative is that changes in session mix or eligibility, rather than case suppression alone, contributed to the case-rate difference.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the causal claim explicitly observational and provide a reproducible cohort definition with session-level linkage, eligibility, authentication, repeat-contact, and downstream-ticket rates by pre/post period and terminal outcome.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "All 4 events have impact_mw=0" and the evidence table identifies inverter_events.csv fields impact_mw, inverter_id, and event_ts.
"Event durations range from 1 to 7 minutes, and all 4/4 events are marked cleared=yes," with the cited duration_min and cleared fields.
The submission distinguishes observation from inference by stating that zero impact "could reflect a genuine absence of impact or a default/exported value."

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The analyst uses multiple supplied fields—impact_mw, duration_min, cleared, severity, and event_type—to assess whether escalation is warranted.
The proposed SCADA check tests the plausible innocent explanation that impact_mw is an export/default value rather than an observed operating value.
The reasoning is based primarily on one event extract; the independent SCADA cross-check is proposed rather than already performed.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Low that it currently represents a real operational anomaly" while assigning "Medium" confidence that one cheap verification is worthwhile.
"This does not prove that no underlying failure occurred outside the export."
The conditional conclusion specifies what evidence would change the decision: non-zero impact, prolonged disturbance, or inconsistent telemetry.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: "Perform one cheap, read-only verification and otherwise stop."
The action is narrowly targeted to INV-17 at 2026-05-27 09:42 and preserves operational safety by recommending no equipment action or source-data change.
The escalation trigger is specific to evidence from the underlying record rather than to the warning label alone.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion—one inexpensive verification followed by no escalation if SCADA confirms zero impact and clearance—matches the short, cleared, zero-impact event evidence.
The submission appropriately avoids inferring equipment failure, intent, or commercial impact from the supplied extract.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The phrase "four consecutive zero-impact values" is potentially overstated unless the source establishes temporal consecutiveness; four events in an extract do not necessarily constitute a consecutive sequence.

The claim that there are "no missing values in the supplied event fields" is acceptable only if every relevant field was checked; the cited table does not enumerate a completeness check for each field.
"No failure event" is a defensible description of the supplied extract, but should remain scoped to the export rather than to plant reality; the submission mostly makes that scope clear.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The impact_mw field may be a default or export artifact, while the COMM_LINK_WARN was a transient communications issue with no production impact. A less likely but decision-relevant alternative is that telemetry or production impact occurred outside the exported event record; the proposed raw SCADA/historian check discriminates between these interpretations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Perform the proposed read-only SCADA/historian check for INV-17 around 2026-05-27 09:42, specifically comparing raw inverter output, communications state, and event-clear time against the exported impact_mw value.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `dispatch_blocks.csv` and specific DSM totals for the 31.6% reduction, and explicitly shows the arithmetic for the generation-gap discrepancy.
It identifies `schedule_source` as the basis for the 12/96 `pilot_revision` and 84/96 `qca_base` split.
Some claims, such as 'comparable high-wind operating conditions and high availability,' are referenced to fields but are not demonstrated with the actual field values or a comparison.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission correctly states that 'one treated day versus one comparator day' leaves weather, forecast accuracy, operating conditions, and other day-specific factors confounded.
It distinguishes the observed reduction from a causal estimate and uses both dispatch data and the commercial settlement description.

However, the alternatives are mostly listed rather than tested, and it does not actually perform or describe the required 29-May block-level comparison using `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw`.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission clearly says the 31.6% is 'an observed one-day penalty reduction, not a causal pilot impact.'
It identifies the unknown conventional-schedule penalty under the same realized 29-May conditions and separately flags the unreconciled generation-gap metric.
The proposed decision transition is conditional on repeated shadow comparisons rather than on the headline result alone.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to 'continue controlled/shadow evaluation only' and avoid national expansion is proportionate to the causal uncertainty.
The proposed read-only, reversible test preserves operational and accounting constraints.
The next test is sensible but delayed to 'the next comparable high-wind event' instead of first extracting the available same-day counterfactual from the 29-May schedule fields.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly preserves the observed benefit while rejecting the claim that 31.6% proves causation.
It appropriately keeps expansion on hold rather than discarding the result entirely.

It does not quantify or use the smaller same-day counterfactual benefit required by comparing `base_schedule_mw` with `submitted_schedule_mw` on 29 May, so the conclusion is directionally right but incomplete.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Observed: The 31.6% DSM reduction is supported by the cited 28-May and 29-May penalty totals in `dispatch_blocks.csv`.
Inferred and appropriately qualified: The different-day comparison is not causal because day-specific conditions remain confounded.
Observed: The 12/96 versus 84/96 schedule-source split is supported by the cited `schedule_source` field.
Partly supported but under-demonstrated: 'comparable high-wind operating conditions and high availability' is asserted without showing the underlying field comparison.
Observed: The submission's arithmetic demonstrates that the stated generation-gap figures do not equal the displayed Schedule minus Generation values.

Overstated or incomplete: 'if repeated shadow comparisons show a persistent penalty reduction attributable to the pilot' assumes attribution without specifying how repeated events will control for event-selection and other changing conditions.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The lower 29-May penalty may be a day-specific result caused by weather, forecast accuracy, operating conditions, or the fact that only 12 blocks used `pilot_revision`, rather than a pilot effect. A same-day comparison of the 29-May `base_schedule_mw` and `submitted_schedule_mw` against the same realized meter data could preserve the evidence of a smaller benefit without treating 31.6% as causal.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Perform and report the 29-May block-level counterfactual now: calculate DSM settlement under `base_schedule_mw` and compare it with settlement under `submitted_schedule_mw` using the same realized generation and meter data, including the resulting effect size and which blocks drive it.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission ties the declaration facts to `declaration.pdf`: "P1001 uses **90211000**, US origin, **CHF 126,900**, duty **0%**, Preference No, Accepted, dated **4 Nov 2025**."
It identifies the relevant comparison sources: "Helios maps **P1001 → 90211090**" and "Swiss matrix maps **P1001 → 90211000**, effective **1 Jul 2025**."
Limitation: the submission does not provide row numbers, quoted source passages, matrix version, or the exact product-description linkage supporting the matrix mapping.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: It explicitly tests the central competing hypothesis: "The declaration is wrong because it differs from Helios." — rejected because "the Swiss matrix independently supports **90211000** for the applicable period."

It correctly rejects overreliance on status: "Accepted status proves the classification is legally correct." — rejected because "acceptance establishes processing status, not independent legal validation."
It preserves a conditional decision rule: "If Tares gives another tariff number, **escalate CH-2025-000522 for classification review**."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The conclusion is qualified: "This supports a **cross-jurisdiction mapping exception**, not demonstrated misdeclaration."
It identifies a precise unresolved issue: "The remaining unknown is whether authoritative Swiss Tares supports **90211000 for P1001 on 4 Nov 2025**."
It acknowledges a source limitation: "the matrix is not final legal proof."
It avoids treating acceptance as conclusive: "acceptance establishes processing status, not independent legal validation."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission explains the jurisdiction/code mechanism: "Swiss Tares uses 8-digit Swiss tariff numbers: the first **6 digits** are the HS component and the final **2** are Swiss subheadings. Thus an identical 8-digit code across jurisdictions is not required."
It recognizes data-context dependencies: "jurisdiction/version/effective-date context matters."
It connects timing to the case: the Swiss mapping is effective "**1 Jul 2025**" before the "**4 Nov 2025** declaration."
Limitation: it does not fully establish the underlying product-description equivalence or explain the provenance, governance, and version lineage of the Helios and Swiss matrix mappings.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The proposed action is narrow and proportionate: "Perform one cheap, narrow, read-only Tares validation for P1001 on **4 Nov 2025**."
It avoids premature operational changes: "Do not amend/re-file the declaration or change master/matrix data."
It defines safe outcomes: "If classification cannot be established, **keep it unresolved** rather than treating either code as proven."
It provides an escalation trigger tied to evidence: "If Tares gives another tariff number, **escalate CH-2025-000522 for classification review**."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "P1006 is not relevant here" is asserted without showing the underlying case evidence establishing why P1006 can be excluded.
The statement that "Swiss Tares uses 8-digit Swiss tariff numbers" is not tied to a cited source in the evidence table, although it may be correct.
The characterization that the check is "reversible" and "cheap" is plausible but not evidenced from the supplied materials.
The overall "Confidence is high" is somewhat stronger than the evidence warrants because the matrix is acknowledged not to be final legal proof and the authoritative Tares result remains unknown.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Swiss matrix could be stale, non-authoritative, incorrectly linked to P1001, or based on a different product description or nomenclature version; consequently, 90211000 could still be an incorrect declaration code despite the apparent jurisdictional mismatch. The submission appropriately preserves this possibility through the Tares validation condition.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Quote or identify the exact rows, matrix version, product description, and effective-date record showing that the Swiss matrix's 90211000 entry applies to the same P1001 and nomenclature version as the 4 November 2025 declaration.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Run one narrow, read-only documentary verification: retrieve the current P1006 supplier declaration and the exact preferential rule/proof used for the 18 Sep 2025 claim, then check validity and shipment applicability."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The submission states that the air waybill "links the shipment to the declaration, supporting document/shipment identity," but provides no page, field, or quoted waybill text demonstrating that linkage.

The conclusion that acceptance "does not independently prove origin entitlement" is well calibrated, but the submission does not cite the governing customs or preferential-origin rule establishing that evidentiary limitation.

The evidence table uses file-level citations rather than exact pages, rows, fields, or passages, so the reported dates, status, duty rate, and register validity cannot be independently audited from the submission alone.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preference claim may still be valid: a supplier declaration or other permitted proof could exist outside the searched register or packet, and the register's 31 Jul 2025 expiry and absence of a current reference demonstrate a gap in the supplied evidence rather than invalidity or fraud. The analyst appropriately preserves this possibility and requests shipment-specific proof.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add exact page, row, field, or quoted-passage citations for each decisive declaration, invoice, waybill, and supplier-register fact, and identify the applicable preferential arrangement and rule so the requested supplier proof can be tested against a defined legal requirement.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "obtain the authoritative evidence-availability timestamp and disposition-time CoA/deviation state"
"This is a cheap, narrow, reversible verification and directly tests the only missing measurement needed for the decision."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that the authoritative required_evidence_available_ts is the "only missing measurement needed" is too strong: the analysis should also test timestamp semantics, especially whether qcore_release_ts is an interface commit rather than a decision time, and should profile the release timestamp distribution.
The response does not substantiate or address the extreme concentration of qcore_release_ts around 02:10, which could indicate batch/interface timing rather than workflow completion.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent long cycle may be driven primarily by interface or scheduled-release timing: qcore_release_ts could represent an enterprise release commit rather than the underlying disposition decision, with the 02:10 concentration being a key diagnostic signal. Source freshness and non-coherent snapshots could further distort joins and apparent status at release.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add a timestamp-semantics test before sampling KPI compliance: profile qcore_release_ts by hour and obtain the event/decision log or data dictionary defining evidence availability, disposition, and QCore release timestamps. This would distinguish genuine workflow delay from an interface-timing artifact and prevent optimizing the wrong KPI.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The 24 open requests total $152,558.03" sourced to `part_requests.csv`, `spare_parts.csv`, and `part_restrictions.csv`; candidate rows identify specific requests, parts, revisions, sites, quantities, and statuses.
"MaintStar-global is a monthly 26 Jun 2026 snapshot, while restrictions are dated 30 Jul 2026" sourced to `source_freshness.csv` and `part_restrictions.csv`.

The evidence is generally traceable and includes counterevidence such as PR-260700 reserved stock and PR-260705 revision mismatch, but it does not provide row-level identifiers or a complete audit trail for all 24 classifications.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Semantic search creates candidates, not transfer approvals" and "transfer eligibility also depends on identity, revision, UOM, qualification, reservation and current availability."

The submission tests multiple alternatives: semantic similarity, exact MPN, revision mismatch, reservation, and stale global availability, and distinguishes retrieval from operational transferability.
"What Would Change the Decision" identifies observations that would discriminate between live availability, engineering equivalence, revision approval, and non-transferability.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "The global inventory snapshot is stale, so an apparently clean match is not yet a transfer approval."

The submission uses confidence labels and explicitly identifies the freshness conflict, but still labels several matches "Actionable now" even though live availability has not been confirmed; that category is more certain than the evidence supports.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Treat search results as candidates, not automatic transfers."
"Do not reserve, transfer, purchase, or alter inventory records; the validation is reversible."

The recommendation is operationally safe and proposes read-only validation, but the "Actionable now" classification should be reframed as conditionally actionable or pending live confirmation given the stale inventory snapshot.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "A semantic description match means the part is transferable" — rejected because revision, UOM, qualification and reservation can invalidate them.
"Exact MPN means immediate transfer" — rejected using PR-260700 reserved stock and PR-260705 revision mismatch.
"Global available quantity is current free stock" — rejected because the global snapshot is dated 26 Jun 2026 and may lag local reservation.
These are plausible alternatives actively tested against examples, although the submission does not fully explore other explanations for stale or conflicting quantity records.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "The smallest verification is one read-only check of live reservation/available-to-transfer status plus receiving-engineering equivalence."

The requested evidence is prioritized, specific, reversible, and tied to decision transitions; it could be improved by separating the highest-value first query—live availability—from engineering review for candidates that survive that check.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The claim that $26,453.52 is "Actionable now" is overstated because availability relies on a 26 Jun 2026 global snapshot while restrictions are dated 30 Jul 2026; the evidence supports candidate or conditionally actionable status pending a live check.

"Current evidence classifies" the four exact matches as actionable without showing the underlying rows or proving that storage, shelf-life, local reservation, and available-to-transfer status are current for each one.

The claim that one verification consisting of live inventory plus engineering equivalence is sufficient may omit other policy gates such as qualification, UOM, revision approval, and shelf-life where those remain unresolved.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The semantic-search process may have generated valuable exact-identity candidates, but none should be treated as actionable now until the stale global inventory is reconciled with live reservation and available-to-transfer data; the correct current output may therefore be candidate value of $152,558.03 and conditionally actionable value of $26,453.52, rather than confirmed actionable value.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Reclassify all matches dependent on the stale MaintStar snapshot as "pending live availability confirmation," then obtain a read-only live available-to-transfer and reservation extract keyed by manufacturer part number, revision, site, and UOM before calling any value actionable.
